dims.summary:
Read-only review of process, priority, approval and tooling rules. I fully read AGENTS.md, docs/RELEASE_PLAN.md, docs/HANDOFF_CODEX.md (all 284 lines), docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/ART_DIRECTION.md, docs/ART_PROMPTS.md and .claude/settings.local.json. CLAUDE.md does not exist. I checked the key claims with git diff/log/show, the tool sources (gen_images.sh, build_place.py, sync_to_studio.py, playtest.py, studio_mcp.py) and greps of the place file. The repo has 17 real conflicts or stale rules.

The four most dangerous:
1. **Work order.** The newest "game first" order clashes with the beta list, which still says "이 순서로" and puts avatar eye blur first as "최우선". The game-first paragraph is uncommitted and newer than commit 85f180b, so it should win.
2. **Image tool.** Every image rule still names GPT, Codex or GPT Pro: AGENTS, SPEC_ADDENDUM A14-3, RELEASE_PLAN, HANDOFF and gen_images.sh. The user cancelled Codex on 2026-10-05 and moved to Firefly, and no doc records this.
3. **Commits.** Hard rule 5 says "Commit + push to main after each meaningful round" with no file-selection limit. Only HANDOFF bans `git add -A`. `.tripo/` is not in .gitignore. The modified place/GoodEvil.rbxlx is half-integrated: it has the new shop code but none of the manual-combat or tutorial code.
4. **PC shutdown.** HANDOFF §3 still tells the worker to shut down the user's computer after finishing, and to use a Codex usage reset. This was an expired overnight-session order.

Other findings:
- There is no overall precedence ladder, and six HANDOFF headings each claim to be "최신".
- Older screen-control notes are looser than Hard rule 6. The Studio MCP input tools are not covered by any rule.
- sync_to_studio.py and playtest.py silently stop the user's Play session. The persona rule says to announce restarts first.
- build_place.py with no arguments overwrites the 12.5 MB Studio place file.
- Old blanket permissions are still written down: "내 허락 안 받아두 돼" and a 425-credit cap.
- "Never invent styling in code" conflicts with the need to build new game-first screens before the user picks their art.
- GDD and the weapon decision doc say "root가 진행 중" for Studio verification. RELEASE_PLAN and A22 say verification resumes 2026-10-06. "Root" is no longer defined.
- "Claude가 결과를 따로 다시 검사한다" assumed Codex was the worker. A Claude worker would end up checking its own results.
- Stale state: GraphicsMode restore, 1/18 vs 2/18 avatars, "ShopService WIP 미적용", the archer HOLD, and the merchant art being called unapproved.
- ART_DIRECTION still specifies AUTO, PERFECT and charge-ring UI and bans asset IDs.
- docs/HANDOFF.md is an old prompt addressed to Claude Code that bans pushing to main and lists auto-charge as a locked decision.

"No explanations" vs "report solved counts" is not a real conflict.
checked_ok: "No explanations" (AGENTS.md:14) vs "report solved/total counts" (AGENTS.md:21, :35): not contradictory. Both ask for short Korean result reports; counts are part of the brief result.

Persona line AGENTS.md:30 (observe play via Studio MCP screen/log/state) is consistent with Hard rule 6: AGENTS.md:46 explicitly allows `tools/studio_mcp.py` `screen_capture`. Desktop computer-use remains banned.

Manual combat precedence is stated explicitly and consistently in AGENTS.md:10, RELEASE_PLAN.md:11, GDD.md §0-2 (line 36+), SPEC_ADDENDUM.md:5 (A22 overrides A1-A21/TECH_SPEC) and HANDOFF_CODEX.md:5. GDD no longer lists auto-charge.
Approved FreshTyped faction card lock is consistent: AGENTS.md:20, HANDOFF_CODEX.md:24, RELEASE_PLAN.md:7 ("승인된 그림을 유지하고 새 카드 생성·교체는 보류").
Release dates are consistent: AGENTS.md:6-7, RELEASE_PLAN.md:22-24 (freeze 10/24, beta 10/31 11:00 KST, launch 12/19), HANDOFF_CODEX.md:53.
RELEASE_PLAN over HANDOFF task order is explicit in both AGENTS.md:5 and RELEASE_PLAN.md:3.
Moderation and upload rules (Hard rule 1, never upload art/out/v1, batches of 10 or fewer, show the user first) match HANDOFF_CODEX.md:227 and :247.
Secrets: .env is in .gitignore. Hard rule 4 is consistent with HANDOFF_CODEX.md:13 (".env·.tripo/는 커밋하지 않는다"); only .tripo/ is missing from .gitignore (see the commit finding).

The 2026-10-06 resume date is consistent across RELEASE_PLAN.md:13, SPEC_ADDENDUM.md:13 and HANDOFF_CODEX.md:13. Only GDD.md:28 and the weapon decision doc still say "root 진행 중" (see the root finding).

The uncommitted Panels.luau diff (tutorial dialog and blacksmith list) reuses `theme.Gold`/`theme.Font` and `UIKit.ArtImage` portraits and adds no new hard-coded Color3/UIStroke styling. Current code practice matches "use existing approved UI".
tools/studio_mcp.py:77 auto-targets the Studio window whose name contains "GoodEvil", so Hard rule 3 (never touch somssi-dev) holds when that wrapper is used.
Paid-API caution for NPC AI dialogue is consistent: GDD.md:25 and weapon_progression_user_decisions:17 both require stating the total first and getting separate approval.

아래 출시 날짜와 베타 필수 목록은 유지하며

findings.explanation:
AGENTS.md:5 and RELEASE_PLAN.md:3 settle RELEASE_PLAN vs the HANDOFF task order. Nothing settles RELEASE_PLAN's own top paragraph (game first: first objective, hunt, loot, blacksmith) against its own beta section, which is still labelled "이 순서로" with eye blur as "최우선".

Git dating: the beta list and "최우선" came in with commit 85f180b (2026-10-04 13:25). The game-first paragraph is uncommitted and was written after 9f71510 (16:14), so it is newer.

The eye-blur work is 3D avatar art, which the game-first rule defers. It is pending a paid Tripo approval (95 credits) and clashes with "Keep the original 3D avatars intact". HANDOFF §3 item 1 is also stale: the archer was already promoted (HANDOFF:110).

The beta must-have scope and the 10/24 freeze stay valid. Only the order is in question.
findings.failure_scenario: On 2026-10-06 the worker reads "베타 필수 — 이 순서로 … (최우선)" or HANDOFF:56/§3 item 1. It spends the first days on avatar face and Tripo work, or asks for paid approval, instead of the first-10-minutes gameplay loop the user chose last.
findings.suggested_fix:
RELEASE_PLAN.md:37 → "## 베타(10/31) 필수 범위 — 작업 순서는 위 '현재 진행 순서'(게임성 먼저)를 따른다".

RELEASE_PLAN.md:38 → "1. 캐릭터 눈·세부 번짐 해결 후 직업 아바타 18종 연결 (첫 10분 게임성 흐름 검증 뒤 진행. 유료 Tripo는 총액을 알리고 사용자 새 승인 필요)".

HANDOFF_CODEX.md:249 → "## 3. 다음에 할 일 (2026-10-04 오전 기록 — 현재 순서는 RELEASE_PLAN 상단과 이 문서 맨 위 '최신 인계')".

HANDOFF_CODEX.md:56: append "(이후 '게임성 먼저' 결정으로 후순위)".

The reviewer should also tell the user that eye blur is no longer first, given the 10/24 freeze, and let them confirm.
findings.verifier_note: The core conflict is real. RELEASE_PLAN.md:37-38 says "이 순서로 … (최우선)" (added in 85f180b at 13:25). The game-first paragraph at :7 is uncommitted and newer, and so is HANDOFF:13. AGENTS.md:5 makes RELEASE_PLAN beat HANDOFF:13, so a strict reading puts eye-blur first. Two corrections: (1) The 95cr is not pending. HANDOFF:62 says R1 already spent 95cr ("아래 예전 '95 승인 대기/유료0'는 당시 기록이다"). The open paid gate is R2/G2 (HANDOFF:66: free B0H reuse at 0cr, or a new candidate at 215–275cr), which HANDOFF:56 puts on hold. (2) AGENTS.md:22 ("in this design pass") and RELEASE_PLAN:17 limit the 3D-avatar exclusion to the 2D redraw, so they do not clash with beta item #1. The point that HANDOFF:251 is stale is correct: HANDOFF:110 records the archer as promoted.

findings.title: All image-generation rules still mandate GPT/Codex ("GPT Pro: generate freely", gen_images.sh, SPEC A14-3); Codex was cancelled 2026-10-05 and Firefly replaces it

locations.quote: **All visual design is done with GPT image generation** (you can generate images natively).
The user has GPT Pro: generate images freely.
`bash tools/gen_images.sh <ids...>` (Git Bash) — Codex image batch
CODEX="${CODEX:-$HOME/.codex/plugins/.plugin-appserver/codex.exe}"
Every visual design is generated by GPT (Codex image generation, art/prompts → art/out)
Codex는 답안과 체크리스트를 준비만 한다.
게임 아이콘과 썸네일: GPT 시안을 보여 주고 사용자가 고른다.
모든 디자인은 GPT 그림으로 먼저(사용자가 고름) → 그대로 구현.
새로운 상점/NPC 시각 디자인은 기존 규칙대로 GPT 시안을 먼저 보여 준다.
must each be generated individually as transparent PNGs from the start
Release dates and paid-work approval rules remain unchanged.

findings.explanation:
No doc records the 2026-10-05 cancellation. Problems a Claude worker will hit:
- Claude cannot "generate images natively".
- gen_images.sh shells out to codex.exe.
- SPEC_ADDENDUM is declared "authoritative" (AGENTS.md:55), so A14-3 still legally requires GPT/Codex.
- "generate freely" was justified by GPT Pro. Firefly generation uses Adobe generative credits, and AGENTS refers to "paid-work approval rules" without defining them.
- Firefly text-to-image may not output transparent PNGs, so the rule "transparent PNGs from the start" may need generate-then-cut-out for each individual part. Cutting apart full mockups must stay banned.
- Existing approved art is GPT-made, so Firefly candidates need the approved images as style references to keep the "established illustrated style".
- Not decided: who runs Firefly (the user in the web app, or the agent through an attached Adobe connector) and where the files land.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker either runs gen_images.sh (fails: no Codex) and stalls, or tries a different tool and spends Firefly credits freely because the docs say "generate images freely". Alternatively it treats SPEC A14-3 as forbidding non-GPT art and refuses the icon/thumbnail/NPC work in the beta list.
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace AGENTS.md:15-16 with:
"**모든 시각 디자인은 Adobe Firefly로 만든다 (2026-10-05 사용자 결정: Codex 구독 해지).** 승인된 기존 그림을 스타일 참조로 넣어 같은 그림체를 유지한다. 시안을 한 장씩 보여 주고 사용자가 고른 그림만 그대로 구현한다. 코드로 새 시각 스타일을 만들지 않는다. Firefly 크레딧 사용량은 먼저 사용자에게 확인한다(무제한 생성 허락 없음). 기존 GPT/Codex 결과물과 승인 기록은 그대로 보존한다."

Append to AGENTS.md:18: "Firefly가 투명 배경을 바로 못 만들면, 부품을 하나씩 따로 생성한 뒤 배경을 지우는 것은 허용한다. 전체 시안을 잘라 쓰는 것은 계속 금지."

AGENTS.md:66 → "`tools/gen_images.sh`는 Codex 전용이라 사용하지 않는다(해지됨). 프롬프트는 계속 art/prompts/<id>.txt, 결과는 art/out/<id>.png에 저장한다."

Other edits:
- Add a dated note under SPEC_ADDENDUM A14-3: "2026-10-05부터 생성 도구는 Adobe Firefly".
- RELEASE_PLAN.md:26: "Codex는" → "작업 에이전트는"; lines 32/46/57: "GPT" → "Firefly".
- HANDOFF:190 and weapon_progression:22: "GPT" → "Firefly".
- Remove `Bash(codex --version)` from .claude/settings.local.json.

Ask the user who operates Firefly and how files are handed over.
findings.verifier_note: All cited quotes are verified: AGENTS:15/16/66, gen_images.sh:8 (codex.exe), SPEC_ADDENDUM:299, RELEASE_PLAN:26/32/46/57, HANDOFF:190, weapon_progression:22. .claude/settings.local.json allows only "Bash(codex --version)". The reviewer missed that the authoritative ADDENDUM also ties the potion shop to GPT: :799 says "must follow a user-selected GPT image" and :833 keeps MerchantEnabled=false "until GPT Potion_Shop_A is selected". Add both to the rewrite.

findings.title: Hard rule 5 "commit + push after each meaningful round" lacks file selection; conflicts with HANDOFF's verified-files-only/no `git add -A`, HANDOFF.md's no-push-to-main, and .tripo/ is not ignored while the place file is half-integrated

locations.quote: Commit + push to `main` after each meaningful round
삭제·덮어쓰기·`git add -A` 금지. `.env`·`.tripo/`는 커밋하지 않는다.
검증된 파일만 명시해 커밋·push → pull → 첫10분 플레이 순서다
Git 기록은 주 담당자가 처리한다.
main에 직접 푸시하지 마.
기존 `place_update.json`의8개 저장 기록은 최신 통합 저장 증거가 아니다.

findings.explanation:
Rule 5 sits in AGENTS Hard rules (from 2026-10-03). The narrower constraints live only in a HANDOFF note, and nothing states that one overrides the other.

Verified state:
- `git status` shows 21 tracked modified files plus 204 untracked entries. These include 52 art/out candidates, among them the rejected modular parts.
- `.tripo/` is not in .gitignore.
- place/GoodEvil.rbxlx (modified) contains the new shop code but none of the manual-combat or tutorial code. Grep counts: WeaponOwnedMask 9, SellWeapon 8, BlacksmithVisited 7, all 0 in HEAD; SkillReadyAt, BasicSkill and RequestTutorial 0 in the place file but present in src/.

HANDOFF.md (an old cloud prompt) says the opposite of rule 5 about main.
findings.failure_scenario: After a doc or code round the worker obeys rule 5 literally (`git add -A` or `commit -a`). It commits .tripo/context.json, rejected art candidates and a place file that does not match src/, and pushes to main. A later pull/restore then uses a place without manual combat, or the rejected art looks recorded as shipped.
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace AGENTS.md rule 5 with:
"5. 검증을 마친 라운드마다 해당 파일만 경로를 적어 `git add <path>`로 올리고 main에 커밋·push한 뒤 pull한다. `git add -A`·`git add .`·`git commit -a` 금지. `.env`, `.tripo/`, `build/`, 미승인·거절 `art/out/*` 후보는 커밋하지 않는다. `place/GoodEvil.rbxlx`는 Studio 통합 검증 뒤 build 저장본을 복사했을 때만 커밋한다. 커밋은 작업 세션 하나만 하고 검토 세션은 커밋하지 않는다."

Also add `.tripo/` to .gitignore and mark docs/HANDOFF.md obsolete (see the HANDOFF.md finding).
findings.verifier_note: The facts check out. .tripo/ is not ignored (git check-ignore). There are 21 tracked changes and 204 untracked entries, 52 of them in art/out. The working place file has WeaponOwnedMask 9, SellWeapon 8 and BlacksmithVisited 7 hits (HEAD has 0). SkillReadyAt, BasicSkill, RequestTutorial and AcceptTutorial have 0 hits in the place but exist in src. place and build are byte-identical (sha f0b7568c…). However, rule 5 never says `git add -A`, and HANDOFF:13 narrows it without contradicting it. The only true contradictions are the obsolete HANDOFF.md:52 and HANDOFF:27 ("주 담당자", which overlaps the root-owner finding). It is a gap more than a conflict, so medium.

findings.title: Expired overnight order to shut down the user's computer and use a Codex usage reset is still listed as a 'next step' in HANDOFF §3

locations.quote: 모든 요청이 실제 완료된 뒤에만 사용자의 종료 지시를 실행한다. 사용량3% 조건일 때만 승인된 무료 초기화1회 사용, 자동 유료 구매 금지.
사용자 지시: 전체 요청 실제 완료/저장/커밋/push 뒤 컴퓨터 종료, 미완료 종료 금지.
남은 Codex 사용량3% 때 보유 무료 초기화1회 사용을 조건부 승인했다
전체 요청 실제 완료·저장·커밋/push 뒤 종료

findings.explanation:
These came from the 2026-10-03/04 overnight Codex session. The "Codex usage reset" is meaningless after the cancellation.

The shutdown order sits in §3 "다음에 할 일 (최신 사용자 우선순위)" item 8, which reads as a standing instruction. No later line revokes it. The current way of working (user co-plays, a reviewer session plus a worker session, resume on 10-06) contradicts it.
findings.failure_scenario: At the end of a round a worker decides "all requests complete" and shuts down Windows. This kills Studio (possibly with an unsaved place), the user's play session and the reviewer session.
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace HANDOFF_CODEX.md:258 (§3 item 8) with:
"8. 라운드별 GoodEvil Edit→문법/동기화/Play→저장→place 복사→검증된 파일만 커밋/push. (2026-10-03~04 밤 작업의 '완료 후 컴퓨터 종료'와 'Codex 사용량3% 무료 초기화' 지시는 그 세션에만 해당했고 만료됐다. 사용자가 새로 말하지 않으면 컴퓨터를 끄지 않는다.)"

Prefix lines 119, 160 and 165 with "(만료된 당시 지시)".
findings.verifier_note: The quotes at HANDOFF:119/160/165/258 are verified, and no later line revokes them. The Codex-reset clause is now moot. However, the trigger requires "모든 요청이 실제 완료된 뒤", and many beta must-haves are still open, so the near-term chance of a shutdown is limited. Downgrade to medium; the suggested expiry wording is still worthwhile.

findings.title: No overall precedence ladder; six HANDOFF headings claim "최신" and an old "바꾸면 안 되는 사용자 결정" list still locks auto-charge

locations.quote: `docs/RELEASE_PLAN.md` (user-confirmed 2026-10-04) overrides the HANDOFF task order.
**`docs/SPEC_ADDENDUM.md` (authoritative; A1–A22)**
## 최신 상태: 새 카드3종·설명판 적용, 전체 디자인 재제작 범위 추가
## 최신 우선순위: 출시 계획과 무료 기준선 표시 완료
## 최신 작업 상태 (2026-10-04 05:56 MouthRestored 실제 생산 승격)
### 바꾸면 안 되는 사용자 결정
독창성 7개: 덩치 저울, 원한 돈자루, 자동 장전/손 발사

findings.explanation:
Only two narrow precedence rules exist: RELEASE_PLAN over the HANDOFF task order, and ADDENDUM over TECH_SPEC. Nothing says whether AGENTS Hard rules beat HANDOFF notes, or which HANDOFF section is current.

Headings at lines 3, 22, 36, 49, 82 and 108 all say "최신" although only line 3 is newest. Line 185 calls auto-charge unchangeable; it is overridden only by the combat-specific sentence at AGENTS.md:10. The same gap drives the commit, screen-control, approval and shutdown conflicts in the other findings.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker jumps to a section via grep, for example "최신 작업 상태" at line 108. It acts on 05:56 state (GraphicsMode restore, avatar counts) or on the "바꾸면 안 되는" list, with no rule telling it that section is history.
findings.suggested_fix:
Insert after AGENTS.md:5:
"**충돌 시 우선순위:** ① 사용자의 최신 채팅 지시 ② AGENTS.md Hard rules·사용자 확정 항목 ③ RELEASE_PLAN 상단 '현재 진행 순서' ④ GDD §0, SPEC_ADDENDUM A22(와 이후 최신 A항) ⑤ HANDOFF_CODEX 맨 위 '최신 인계' 한 절 ⑥ 그 아래 HANDOFF 절과 docs/HANDOFF.md는 당시 기록이며 지시가 아니다. 같은 급이면 날짜가 늦은 것이 이긴다."

Rename HANDOFF headings 22/36/49/82/108 to "기록 — <원래 제목> (시각)". Change line 185 to "### 사용자 결정 (2026-10-03 당시; '자동 장전/손 발사'는 2026-10-04 수동 전투로 폐기)".
findings.verifier_note: The six "최신" headings (3/22/36/49/82/108) are real, and no global ladder exists. Correction: the auto-charge lock at HANDOFF:188 is not overridden only by AGENTS:10. HANDOFF:5 names it directly ("아래 과거 기록의 “자동은 장전, 손은 발사” … 현재 요구가 아니다"), and RELEASE_PLAN:11 and SPEC_ADDENDUM:5 also override it. Several sections already carry inline staleness markers (HANDOFF:53, 100, 110, 179). The risk is real but partly mitigated.

findings.title: Older HANDOFF notes describe a looser screen-control regime than Hard rule 6; Studio MCP input tools and studio_id targeting are uncovered for a Claude worker

locations.quote: **No screen control by default (user complaint, 2026-10-04).**
Ask the user first, in Korean, saying what you will click and for how long.

findings.explanation:
Rule 6 (commit cbc3b74, 2026-10-04 12:10) is newer and stricter (ask first, then OK, then one short burst) than HANDOFF:159/180 (turn on when needed, then reset). Rule 6 should win, but HANDOFF does not say so.

The persona's "Studio MCP 화면" is not a conflict, because AGENTS:46 lists screen_capture.

Gaps for a Claude worker:
- It has native Roblox_Studio MCP tools, including user_mouse_input, user_keyboard_input and character_navigation, which inject input. Neither rule 6 nor the persona classifies them.
- Those native tools require an explicit studio_id, while the wrapper auto-picks GoodEvil. This is a Hard rule 3 (somssi-dev) risk.
- Capture needs Studio in the foreground, which requires the user's help.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker follows HANDOFF:180 and turns on desktop control without asking. Or it uses user_mouse_input while the user is playing. Or it calls execute_luau with the first listed studio_id and edits the somssi-dev place.
findings.suggested_fix:
Append to AGENTS rule 6:
"Studio MCP의 user_mouse_input·user_keyboard_input·character_navigation은 사용자 플레이 중에는 쓰지 않고, 그 외에는 검증용으로 짧게만 쓴다. MCP 도구를 직접 쓸 때는 list_roblox_studios에서 이름에 GoodEvil이 든 창의 studio_id만 쓴다(somssi-dev 금지). 캡처가 흰 화면이면 사용자에게 Studio 창을 앞으로 띄워 달라고 부탁한다."

Prefix HANDOFF lines 96, 159 and 180 with "(규칙6 이전 기록 — 지금은 AGENTS 규칙6을 따른다)".
findings.verifier_note: HANDOFF:159 and :180 sit in sections older than cbc3b74 (2026-10-04 12:10), which added rule 6. I checked the native tool schemas: mcp__Roblox_Studio__user_mouse_input, execute_luau and character_navigation all have "studio_id" as a required field, while the wrapper auto-picks a studio whose name contains GoodEvil (studio_mcp.py:77-83). TECH_SPEC:33's stale path (Documents/Game) is correct.

dims.summary:
Read-only review of the game-design contracts (GDD, SPEC_ADDENDUM A1–A22, TECH_SPEC, RELEASE_PLAN, AGENTS.md and the four 2026-10-04 design docs) against Config.luau and the Shop/Quest/Combat/Data/Vitals services, as of uncommitted HEAD 9f71510+21 modified files. Every key number you asked about matches the source: MP20/3s skill, 3-page welcome with explicit accept, 5 slimes for 120 gold, no town slime, tiers 2/3 at 150/800, resale 15/80, shop cap tier 3, tier 1 not sellable, 12-stud anvil, BlacksmithVisited, MerchantEnabled=false, Light heal kept with no charge share, Neutral PvP immunity, and manual-only PvP. The six source files I checked compile with the offline luau-compile.

Rule conflicts that could send a worker the wrong way:
(1) Every design rule still requires GPT/Codex images (AGENTS.md, A14-3, A18-4, a Config comment, RELEASE_PLAN). This now conflicts with the unrecorded 2026-10-05 switch to Adobe Firefly. Beta must-have #3 (the potion merchant) is gated on a "GPT potion-shop preview".
(2) GDD §0-1 and the weapon doc say "Studio verification is in progress by root". GDD §0-2, A22 and HANDOFF say nothing is verified and work resumes 2026-10-06.
(3) The weapon doc says the merchant art is "unapproved, GPT draft in progress", but art/approved.json, GDD and HANDOFF approve merchant C.
(4) TECH_SPEC line 19 forbids `SkillReadyAt`/`UseSkill`, while A22 and the HUD use SkillReadyAt and the skills doc proposes UseSkill.
(5) TECH_SPEC §4.19/§5 still define a zero-argument, sequential UpgradeWeapon and a 5-button HUD with an upgrade button, and say "purchases never go through a remote". The TECH_SPEC banner does not cover the shop, and SPEC_ADDENDUM has no shop contract at all.
(6) RELEASE_PLAN puts crafting after full launch, but GDD §0-1 confirms boss-material crafting with an open schedule.
(7) RELEASE_PLAN keeps "eye blur fix (top priority)" as beta item 1, while the same file and AGENTS.md say gameplay comes first.

Player-facing mismatches with the current rules:
- MP-shortage and empty-potion messages tell players to use or buy potions. The potion merchant is disabled and new players start with 0 bottles, so any class spamming the skill hits this within minutes.
- Old-save rare weapons (tier 4+) cannot be re-equipped once a basic weapon is equipped, despite the "rare weapons preserved" claim.
- The goose reward text still mentions auto attack.

Stale text describing auto attack, charge, PERFECT or "발사" remains in GDD body sections, older SPEC_ADDENDUM sections and the onboarding review doc. Some is not covered by any override (A7-3 upgrade-button text, the A16-13 HaloHealPct key name).

Decisions the user must make before implementing:
- What the next pinned objective is after the blacksmith visit (currently none). This blocks the first 10 minutes.
- How enhancement scrolls work: drop rate, count, success rules, cap. This is the only planned "loot"; today kills give only gold and XP. Blocks the first 10 minutes.
- Potion merchant look, price and panel. Beta must-have.
- Whether new players get the basic skill free, plus slot count and keys.
- How tiers 4–7 are obtained.
- How the equipment-merchant NPC is built (3D work is unapproved).
checked_ok: Basic skill MP20 / 3s: Config.BasicSkill ManaCost=20, Cooldown=3 (Config.luau:294-297); CombatService.Release uses them (lines 825-831), checks MP before committing the cooldown, sets SkillReadyAt; HUD reads Config.BasicSkill.ManaCost (HUD.luau:1871, 2637).

Manual-only combat on the server: Swing returns unless isManual (CombatService.luau:603); Release returns when isAuto (809); SetAutoAttack remote forces AutoAttack=false (1159); Swing/Release reject ClassChosen~=true (606, 812).

Old PvP rule 'auto attacks cannot hit players' is moot: every attack is manual and player targets are gated by CanAttack/Neutral (PvPService.luau:403-404). GDD §5-2 line 183 matches. The A3-M3 AutoUnderAttack hint is no longer sent (Config.Text.AutoUnderAttack has no caller).

Tutorial flow matches GDD §0-2/A22: Config.Tutorial.Welcome has 3 lines per faction for Halo/Horns/Neutral (Config.luau:919-944); RequestTutorial/AcceptTutorial take 0 args (QuestService.luau:335-346); step 0 only opens dialogue; meadow entry moves step 1->2 (748-751); kills count only at step 2 in SlimeMeadow, personal monsters excluded (368-380, 767-774); claim pays 120 bank gold once, setting step 99 first (382-391). QuestService never calls SpawnPersonal. TutorialKills is saved (Config:111) and not reset on rejoin (QuestService:716).

Weapon shop numbers: tier 2/3 prices 150/800 and MinLevel 1/5 (Config.luau:157-158); MaxSoldTier=3 enforced for buy and sell (ShopService.luau:43-53, 112-115); sale proceeds math.floor(price*0.1) = 15/80 (126); tier 1 cannot be sold (101) and is equip-only (62); ownership bit removed before gold is paid (128-130); selling the equipped weapon falls back to tier 1 (129). Panels shows SellPrice floor(Price/10) (Panels.luau:1756), same result.

12-stud anvil gate: CanBuyWeapon uses min(BLACKSMITH.Distance=12, prompt.MaxActivationDistance) for every buy/sell (ShopService.luau:178-192); the blacksmith prompt sets BlacksmithVisited=true only after server validation (194-202).

BlacksmithVisited objective: after the tutorial (step 99) the pinned entry reads 'Config.Tutorial.Text.VisitBlacksmith' until visited (QuestService.luau:409-415); HUD guide beam to the anvil only in Crossroads (HUD.luau:2565-2567).
Config.Vitals.MerchantEnabled=false (Config.luau:33) makes ShopService.CanBuyPotions return false (ShopService.luau:205), so BuyPotion is refused.

Light (Halo) ally heal is kept without charge sharing: only perks.ReleaseSupport==true and fac=='Halo' heal; heal = min(BasicSkill.HaloHealPct*real damage, HaloHealCapPct*MaxHealth); no stack/charge grant remains (CombatService.luau:912-935). Note: the caster heals too (self included), as in the old design.
Neutral rules: ReleaseSupport=false and all perks 0 (Config.luau:382-404); PvPService refuses Neutral either way (403-404); Neutral gets its own welcome dialogue. GDD §5-8 matches.

GDD §6 class numbers (HP/attack/interval/range/targets/move +10%) match Config.Classes (Config.luau:216-266); GDD §2 golden 4% matches Config.Monsters.GoldenChance=0.04; GDD 5-2 'swing ≈5% of base HP' matches PvP.HitPctOfMaxHP 0.10 × SwingImmediate 0.5.
Offline luau-compile exit 0 with no stderr for Config.luau, ShopService, QuestService, CombatService, VitalsService and DataService.

TECH_SPEC lines 3-7 banner and GDD §0-1 line 32 do mark charge/PERFECT/auto/old tutorial and the GDD upgrade-button text as superseded. The stale-doc findings list only text not covered by those notices or easy to misread.

Corrections: RequestTutorial/AcceptTutorial are already specified in A22 (SPEC_ADDENDUM.md:12), and BuyPotion/UsePotion in A18-1 (:775, :794), so the new section only needs the weapon-shop items. The 'hold = repeat' line (:2559) is already overridden by A22:7 under TECH_SPEC.md:24 ('SPEC_ADDENDUM ... overrides this document where they conflict'). findings.title: MP-shortage and empty-potion messages tell players to use or buy potions, but the merchant is disabled and new players have 0 bottles

locations.quote: Net.Notify(player, "MP가 부족해요. MP 물약을 사용해요!", "bad")
Net.Notify(player, "물약이 없어요. 물약 상인에게서 구매해 주세요.", "bad")

현재 없는 아이템·보상을 이미 얻었다고 안내하지 않는다.

findings.explanation: The skill costs 20 MP every 3 s (about 6.7 MP/s) and Mage swings cost 3 MP. Regen is 4 MP/s, so repeated skill use empties MP in well under a minute. The server then tells the player to use an MP potion. With 0 stock it tells them to buy from a potion merchant, but CanBuyPotions always fails while MerchantEnabled=false and no merchant is spawned. The HUD potion buttons also say '구매'. This breaks the GDD/AGENTS rule not to guide players to things that do not exist, inside the first 10 minutes.
findings.failure_scenario: A new player of any class uses the skill a few times in Slime Meadow, gets 'MP가 부족해요. MP 물약을 사용해요!' and taps the MP potion button. They get '물약이 없어요. 물약 상인에게서 구매해 주세요.' and can find no merchant anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Pending the potion-merchant decision, make the messages and button state honest. Example: MP shortage says to wait for MP regeneration and omits potions while MerchantEnabled=false; the empty-stock button shows a disabled 'Not sold yet'-style label, not '구매'. Or give a small starter stock, which needs user approval. Re-enable the purchase wording only together with the merchant.
findings.verifier_note: VitalsService.luau:34 does say 'MP 물약을 사용해요!' to players who have 0 bottles while no merchant exists (MerchantEnabled=false at Config.luau:33). The 0-stock button also shows '구매' (VitalsUI.luau:47). Correction: the second half of the failure scenario does not happen with the normal client. VitalsUI.requestPotion (VitalsUI.luau:56-58) does not fire UsePotion when count<=0, for both the button and keys 1/2 (:115, :214-215). So '물약이 없어요. 물약 상인에게서 구매해 주세요.' (VitalsService.luau:60) only reaches forged requests. The tap just shows '구매' and does nothing. This is real misleading text but limited, so medium.

Config.NextGoal (Config.luau:1554-1559) only gives the Lv10/Lv25 zone guide beam. RELEASE_PLAN.md:15 requires the 10-minute chain to reach '다음 성장 목표'. findings.title: Enhancement scrolls are the planned 'loot', but none of their numbers are decided and kills drop no items

locations.quote: 몬스터가 떨어뜨리는 강화 주문서를 얻고 모아 강화한다.

Prioritize a coherent first objective, combat, loot, meaningful growth and town services.

findings.explanation: AGENTS.md and GDD §0-1 put loot ('전리품') in the first-play chain, and the only defined loot is the enhancement scroll. No scroll, drop or enhance code exists (grep for scroll/주문서 in src finds only the IconScroll art key and UI scroll frames). Kills give only gold and XP. Still undecided: drop rate, scrolls per level, success rule (no destruction/new failure allowed per AGENTS), enhancement cap, stat per level, carry-over when changing tier, guaranteed first drop, inventory/save shape, and whether the first quest reward changes.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker implements the first 10 minutes with no item loot at all, or invents drop rates and success odds without approval, violating 'do not invent undecided values'.

dims.summary:
I reviewed the manual-combat change in CombatService (read in full, plus git diff), Config, Net, VitalsService, ClassService, PvPService, QuestService, KaijuService, GooseService and the client files HUD, Fx, CameraFollow and ClientMain. The core contract holds. One Swing request gives at most one attack, timed by the server's class interval. No server auto-attack or charge loop is left. Release (the skill) checks the cooldown before spending MP, spends MP exactly once and never refunds or re-charges after a rejection. PvP targeting and its protections are unchanged, Halo ally healing still works, and all changed combat-related files compile with luau-compile (exit 0).

Problems found:
- **Release quest farmable (rule conflict):** the quest now counts any skill cast, including misses in a safe town. Dailies and extras can be finished with 3 Q presses. A22 wording says to count skill uses; GDD §0-1 says simplicity must not become free auto-completion.
- **Misleading MP message:** players who run out of MP are told to use MP potions, but potions cannot be bought (merchant disabled, starting stock 0). Mage basic attacks still cost MP from the same pool as the skill.
- **Balance risks:** basic attacks still deal 50% of weapon damage and the other half no longer comes back through charge. In PvP and against the kaiju (the boss form), the skill now reaches its per-cast damage cap every 3 s from a full MP bar, without having to land hits first.
- **Rule conflicts:** the kaiju stomp is still an automatic timed attack against players; neither A22 nor GDD §0-2 says whether it is exempt from "attack only on press". The Horns faction lost its gauge perk with no replacement.
- **Cleanup:** one player-facing message still mentions auto attack, and some leftover constants and dead code remain.

Process note: I first wrote one compiler error file to /tmp/err_combat.txt, outside the scratch folder, then deleted it. Nothing in the repo was changed.
checked_ok: Swing server path: CombatService.Swing returns unless isManual==true (line 603). It rejects players who are not ready, have no class (ClassChosen ~= true), are dead or have no root, or fail the zone gate (attackBlocked) (lines 605-617). It is rate-limited server-side by nextSwingAt = now + class SwingInterval (lines 620-628). onSwingRemote queues at most one press, only within MANUAL_GRACE 0.2 s, and ignores other early repeats (lines 1118-1137). So one request gives at most one attack.

No auto loop remains: AutoLoop/ChargeWatcher and autoTick/chargeTick were removed. CombatService.Start only starts RegenLoop (lines 1222-1230). No server code calls Swing(p,false) or Release(p,true); the only callers are the remote handler and the queue (lines 1113, 1131, 1146).

Release (skill): cooldown is checked before MP (line 828). TrySpendMana is called once with the BasicSkill ManaCost of 20 (line 829). releaseAt and SkillReadyAt are set right after it (lines 830-831), with no rejection point after MP is spent. All rejections (not ready, no class, dead, no root, zone gate, cooldown) happen before spending, so they cost no MP. No stack, charge or PERFECT requirement is left.

Cooldown and MP across lifecycle: a real respawn resets releaseAt, SkillReadyAt and MP together (CombatService 1048-1057, VitalsService 107-113). A cosmetic rig swap keeps both. A class change uses RefreshCharacter (applyStats only, no respawn), so the cooldown and MP carry over. A faction change also keeps the cooldown. pendingManual is cleared on death, class change and faction change.

PvP: the Swing and Release player paths still go through playersNear, which checks PVP_FACTIONS and PvPService.CanAttack: Neutral immunity, same faction, safe zone, rookie, Protected, and the kaiju exception (PvPService 391-423). DamagePlayer keeps its A6 faction guard. Swing PvP damage = 0.5 x ComputePvPHit, the same as the old manual swing. Release 6xD with radius 9 equals the old minimum 10-stack release (0.5*D*10*1.2 = 6D; 8 + 0.1*10 = 9). The 35% player cap and 8% kaiju cap are intact.

Halo skill heal still works (CombatService 912-935, uses BasicSkill HaloHealPct/HaloHealCapPct) and the ally charge share is gone. KaijuService's Released handler still receives info.Healed (KaijuService 638-648).

Leftover remotes and APIs: SetAutoAttack validates a boolean, is rate-limited and always forces AutoAttack=false (lines 1149-1160). No client code fires it any more. GetCharge returns 0. DebugSetCharge is Studio-only and can only zero the attributes. No server code reads the AutoAttack, Charge or PerfectUntil attributes.
Remote argument validation: the Swing and Release handlers ignore every client argument, and isManual/isAuto are hard-coded on the server, so there is no type, NaN or extra-argument path.

Kill attribution: damageMonster -> MonsterService.DamageMonster/killRecord contributor list -> MonsterKilled(player, info with Kind/ZoneId/Golden/Personal) -> QuestService.onMonsterKilled feeds Kill/Golden quests and tutorialKill (step Quest, or Guide inside SlimeMeadow; non-personal SlimeMeadow monsters only). Unchanged by the combat edit.
Goose: RegisterHit is always called with isManual=true (ManualCount 2, rolling cap of 3 per second). Reward eligibility (MIN_MANUAL_HITS) still works.

Client input: F, gamepad R2 and the attack TextButton each send exactly one Swing per press (HUD startHold 2613-2623, no repeat loop). A world click goes through CameraFollow.PrimaryClick and fires only on release when the input was not game-processed and moved less than 6 px; a drag rotates the camera. The attack button is a TextButton, so a button click does not also fire a world click. The R auto key is removed. Q/E/L2 check MP and SkillReadyAt first. Attacks are blocked while Panels or WorldMap is open.
Fx: removed PERFECT / auto-release labels; the Release handler no longer reads Stacks/Perfect/Auto. No dangling ui.auto/ui.ring/ui.charge references in HUD.
luau-compile exit 0, no stderr: CombatService, Config, Net, VitalsService, ClassService, PvPService, QuestService, HUD, Fx, CameraFollow, ClientMain.client, Main.server, KaijuService, GooseService.

locations.quote: local function onReleased(player, info)
addProgress(player, "Release", 1)
CombatService.Released:Fire(player, {
{ Id = "Release", Weight = 20, Units = { 2, 3 }, DailyUnits = { 3 }, RewardPerUnit = 8,

모든 성장을 화면 버튼 하나로 즉시 끝내거나, 반복 노동으로 플레이 시간을 채우지 않는다.

findings.explanation: Previously the Release quest required the release to be fired with 50+ stacks, which meant real fighting. Now Released fires on every accepted cast, including a total miss: MonstersHit=0, PlayersHit=0, cast in a town. onReleased adds 1 without looking at the result. Rerolling a daily keeps it a daily (QuestService 672-678), and a daily pays the full DailyQuestReward (5 min of hunting value). A Release daily (3 units) is therefore 3 presses spread over about 6 s and 60 MP. Release extras pay units*mainGold*8*0.5, about 8-12 kills' worth, for 2-3 presses. The code's own anti-farm intent (killWeight comment: 'cannot be farmed on safe low-zone slimes') and GDD §0-1 say otherwise. A22 only says to count server-recognized manual skill uses.
findings.failure_scenario: A Lv 1 Halo player stands in Crossroads and rerolls a daily every 60 s until it becomes '스킬 3번 사용하기'. They press Q 3 times (about 6 s, no monster nearby), then claim a full daily reward. Repeating this for the 3 dailies also earns the daily chest, all without fighting.
findings.suggested_fix: In onReleased, count only casts where (tonumber(info.MonstersHit) or 0) + (tonumber(info.PlayersHit) or 0) > 0, or require the cast to be outside a town. Ask the user to confirm this reading of A22, then record it in A22.
findings.verifier_note: Every quote checks out. QuestService.luau:783-787 adds 1 per Released event and only skips Auto; CombatService.luau:961-971 fires Released even with MonstersHit=PlayersHit=0. attackBlocked (CombatService.luau:198-234) checks only zone MinLevel and plausibility, so there is no town block. HEAD required stacks >= MinStacks=50 (HEAD Config:931). The old HEAD Halo-share comment explicitly guarded against 'farm Release quests' in a safe town, which supports the reviewer's reading. Feasibility: only one Release quest can sit in the slots at a time (preferred pool excludes existing ids, QuestService.luau:196-205). Even so, a claimed daily becomes an Extra (line 647), and rerolls keep Daily kind (672-678, 60 s cooldown, Config:959), so 3 Release dailies per day without fighting is reachable. Medium is right: the payout is capped per day and is not a gold dupe.

locations.quote: Net.Notify(player, "MP가 부족해요. MP 물약을 사용해요!", "bad")
MerchantEnabled = false, -- enable only after the user selects the GPT potion-shop preview
if Config.Vitals.MerchantEnabled ~= true or typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") then return false end

MageSwingCost = 3,
아직 없는 보상을 안내하거나 완료했다고 보고하지 않는다.

findings.explanation: Swing calls TrySpendMana with silent = not isManual, which is now always false. A Mage whose MP falls below 3 (for example after a 20 MP skill) gets the server toast 'MP 물약을 사용해요!' at most every 2 s. But the potion merchant is disabled and potion stock starts at 0 and cannot be bought (ShopService rejects the purchase), so the message points to something unavailable. Separately, Mage basic attacks drain 2.4 MP/s (3 MP per 1.25 s) against 4 MP/s regen. A Mage who keeps attacking therefore recovers 20 MP in about 12.5 s, versus about 5 s for Warrior or Archer. GDD §0-2 and A22 only describe MP for skills, not for basic attacks.
findings.failure_scenario: A new Mage casts the skill at 21 MP, leaving 1 MP. The next F press is rejected and shows 'MP가 부족해요. MP 물약을 사용해요!'. The player has no potions and no way to buy any.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the message to drop the potion advice while MerchantEnabled is false (for example 'MP가 부족해요. 잠시 후 회복돼요.'), or make it depend on CanBuyPotions. Ask the user whether Mage basic attacks should still cost MP under the manual design, and record the answer in A22.
findings.verifier_note: Real part: VitalsService.luau:34 tells the player to use MP potions, but MerchantEnabled=false (Config.luau:33) and potion stock has no other source (only the HPPotionCount/MPPotionCount defaults of 0 and ShopService). Same problem at VitalsService.luau:60 ('물약 상인에게서 구매해 주세요'). In practice the toast only reaches Mage F presses, because the client blocks Q below 20 MP with its own 'MP가 부족해요.' (HUD.luau:2637-2638). Corrections: (1) the toast is not new; HEAD manual swings were already non-silent. (2) Mage basic-attack MP is documented: SPEC_ADDENDUM.md:767 'MageSwingCost=3' (A18-1) and HANDOFF_CODEX.md:205 '마법사 공격3MP'. A22 keeps the rest, so the claim that the docs only describe MP for skills is wrong, and no new user question is needed for that part.

findings.title: Basic attacks still deal only 50% of weapon damage; the other half used to come back through charge, which no longer exists

locations.quote: local dealt = Util.RoundDamage(d * ((Config.BasicSkill and Config.BasicSkill.SwingImmediate) or 0.5))
SwingImmediate = 0.5, PvPCapPct = 0.35, HaloHealPct = 0.10, HaloHealCapPct = 0.30,
-- Damage = normal per-target swing damage at Lv 1 for class Damage multiplier 1.0, BEFORE the 50% immediate rule.

findings.explanation: In the old design a hit dealt 0.5xD immediately and also earned stacks that came back as release damage. Removing charge kept the 0.5 multiplier but removed the payback path. A player who only presses F now deals half the documented 'normal per-target' damage. Examples: Warrior Lv 1 tier 1 deals 4 per hit and needs 3 hits on a 10 HP slime; a Goblin (90 HP) at around Lv 10 with tier 2 takes about 11 Warrior hits. The skill (6xD for 20 MP) is the only way to make up the difference. This is a balance change that A22 does not mention, and it directly affects first-10-minute pacing.
findings.failure_scenario: A new player who ignores Q hunts the 5 tutorial slimes and the next zone at about half the old baseline damage, so the hunt -> loot -> weapon loop feels slow.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the basic-attack multiplier on purpose for manual combat: raise BasicSkill.SwingImmediate, or document 0.5 as intended. Confirm in the 10-06 Studio playtest and record the value in A22.
findings.verifier_note: CombatService.luau:731/750 apply BasicSkill.SwingImmediate=0.5 (Config.luau:296), carried over unchanged from Config.Charge.SwingImmediate. The per-stack payback (addCharge on hit) was removed in this diff. Slime HP 10 (Config.luau:881) against Warrior Lv1 T1 at 8*0.5=4 means 3 hits, as stated. A22 and GDD §0-2 never restate the 0.5 rule; only the Config.luau:152 comment does. This is a valid playtest and decision item for first-10-minute pacing.

findings.title: Skill damage against players and the kaiju is no longer gated by landed hits; the per-cast cap is reachable every 3 s from a full MP bar

locations.quote: local raw = math.min(D * releaseMult, capPct * vHum.MaxHealth)
ManaCost = 20, Cooldown = 3, DamageMultiplier = 6, Radius = 9,
HitPctOfMaxHP = 0.10, -- normal per-target PvP hit = victim BASE MaxHealth * 0.10 * powerRatio * ... (§4.9)
ReleaseCapPct = 0.08, -- CR-M7: one release on an ACTIVE kaiju deals <= 8% of its current MaxHealth (players: Charge.PvPCapPct)

findings.explanation: PvP D is about 10% of the victim's max HP x power ratio (0.8-1.5) x class Damage, so 6xD is roughly 48-90% for Warrior and Mage, always clipped to the 35% cap. Before, each release needed at least 10 stacks, about 5 landed manual hits for a Warrior. Now a full 100 MP bar allows casts at t=0, 3, 6 s, an AoE of 35% each: an enemy at full HP dies in about 6 s from skills alone, before swing damage. Against an Active kaiju, each Halo player can deal 8% every 3 s for the first ~5 casts, so a group burst is roughly twice the old rate. Only the cadence changed, not the formula.
findings.failure_scenario: A Warrior or Mage walks into a PvP zone and casts the skill three times on a radius-9 group of enemy players. Every enemy in range loses 105% of max HP in 6 s without the attacker landing a single basic hit.
findings.suggested_fix: Playtest PvP and kaiju time-to-kill on 10-06. If it is too fast, add a lower PvP cap or a separate PvP skill multiplier (for example BasicSkill.PvPDamageMultiplier). Record the chosen values in A22.
findings.verifier_note: The cap math is correct: CombatService.luau:899, BasicSkill 6x, PvPCapPct 0.35, Kaiju ReleaseCapPct 0.08 (Config.luau:588). Corrections: (1) the formula did change. HEAD used Config.ReleaseDamage = 0.5*D*n*(1+0.02n), which equals 6D only at n=10; the new value is a fixed 6D. Only the caps are the same. (2) HEAD releases also cost 20 MP (HEAD Release called TrySpendMana(Config.Vitals.ReleaseCost)). (3) Stacks could be pre-built on monsters, plus Halo got +10 stacks from allies, so even the old first PvP release needed no landed PvP hit. Real net change: a skill every 3 s instead of about every 5 hits (about 5 s for Warrior). Old time-to-kill with swings was already about 5 s, so the increase is modest. Keep it as a 10-06 playtest item, not a medium risk.

findings.title: Kaiju stomp is still an automatic, timer-driven attack on players; A22 and GDD §0-2 do not say whether it is exempt

findings.explanation: Every StompInterval (4 s), an Active kaiju player automatically damages Halo players within 15 studs, credited to the kaiju in PvP zones. The kaiju player never presses anything for this. It is an event mechanic, but the new rule reads 'attack only on press' with no exception. findings.verifier_note: Quotes are verified (KaijuService.luau:457, 572; AGENTS.md:10). The stomp is a documented kaiju-form mechanic (TECH_SPEC.md:2172-2173, Config.luau:575-577). dims.summary:
I checked the guide dialogue, first mission and persistence by reading the code and git diffs, and by running the existing offline fixture in my scratch folder against the current sources. In the source tree the server-side flow is correct:
- Both tutorial remotes take no arguments and are validated.
- Closing the dialogue does not accept the mission.
- Kills or travel before acceptance do not count.
- Only Slime and BigSlime killed in Slime Meadow count, and personal monsters are excluded.
- The reward is exactly 120 bank gold, paid once, because the step is set to 99 before the gold is added and nothing yields in between.
- Progress is now saved in `TutorialKills` (a default, normalized on load and saved with the whole record) along with `TutorialStep`, which is mirrored to the player.
- Legacy saves are migrated safely.

All 10 relevant Luau files compile with luau-compile. With the current sources, including the newer Config, the fixture passes 459 checks; 4 extra probes I wrote also ran.

No blocker was found. The main risks:
1. `place/GoodEvil.rbxlx` and `build/GoodEvil.rbxlx` still hold an intermediate tutorial with no guide dialogue. Studio must be synced before testing, and that place file must not be committed as it is.
2. SPEC_ADDENDUM A4 and A5-C4 still say "every step is skippable" and describe the personal slime. A22's closing line only says it replaces combat-related rules, so this is a real rule conflict.
3. After the reward the player has about 135 gold, but the next weapon costs 150. Once the shop is opened, no pinned goal remains until the Lv10 zone guide. This is arithmetic from Config, not a playtest result.

Smaller issues:
- `TutorialKills` is not reset when the mission is re-accepted. My probe showed a second 120-gold payout, but only after a Studio debug or manual reset of the step.
- The evidence doc `onboarding_offline_review.md` describes the old flow.
- Every finished player is republished once a second.
- Unused personal-slime code and config remain.
- Stale "blocked upload" comments sit on portrait ids that were already re-uploaded under the new account.

The cancelled Codex subscription (images now from Adobe Firefly) does not touch this area: the first mission needs no new images.
checked_ok: Zero-arg remotes: QuestService onRequestTutorial/onAcceptTutorial reject any payload (select('#', ...) ~= 0), then canWelcome checks Player instance + Parent == Players + Util.IsAlive + ready data (getData uses PlayerService.IsReady) + ClassChosen + valid Class + step == 0 + faction Welcome table, then Util.RateLimit 0.5s (QuestService.luau:319-346). Client Panels.fire packs exact args, so FireServer() sends zero (Panels.luau:667-675, 1193, 1259).

Closing is not acceptance: the Later button and panel close only call Panels.Close (Panels.luau:1198-1200). The server step changes only through AcceptTutorial. The client closes the dialogue when TutorialStep becomes non-zero and shows a retry message after 5s without confirmation.

Pre-acceptance kills or travel do not count: onMonsterKilled/onZoneChanged/tryTutorial do nothing toward the mission at step 0. A step-1 kill in the meadow before ZoneChanged moves to step 2 and counts that kill (QuestService.luau:748-775).

Kill attribution: TUTORIAL_KINDS = MonsterTypes with Zone 'SlimeMeadow' (Slime, BigSlime only). Requires info.ZoneId == 'SlimeMeadow' and Personal ~= true. MonsterService.killRecord supplies ZoneId and Personal (MonsterService.luau:1038-1047). CR-M5 means the player must be in the meadow to damage meadow monsters. A golden meadow slime counts as one kill (scratch probe).

120 gold exactly once: claimTutorial requires step 2 and 5 kills, sets step 99 before AddBankGold with no yield in between. AddBankGold adds the exact amount with no faction bonus. Repeated claims, rejoins and same-frame duplicates pay nothing more (fixture plus code read). Cross-server double claims are blocked by the DataService session lock and token.

Persistence: Config.Data.Defaults.TutorialKills = 0. DataService.fillDefaults clamps it to 0..5 and repairs NaN/inf/strings. DataService.writeRecord deep-copies the whole session table, so TutorialKills, BlacksmithVisited and WeaponOwnedMask are saved. TutorialStep is mirrored. onPlayerReady no longer resets progress.

Migration: a stored record without TutorialStep becomes 99 before the default fill. Unknown or invalid steps (3, -1, NaN, inf) become 99. Brand-new records start at 0. A legacy step 0 (old personal-slime era) now gets the dialogue. Legacy steps 1 and 2 resume, with kills starting at 0 because the old count was session-only.
No town slime: QuestService no longer calls MonsterService.SpawnPersonal, and grep finds no remaining caller in src/.

Per-faction dialogue: Config.Tutorial.Welcome has Halo, Horns and Neutral, each with a name and 3 Korean lines. Faction 'None' gets no dialogue. The menu entry '안내자 만나기' appears only while step 0 and class chosen (Panels.luau:1230-1232), matching Text.Welcome '첫 임무 · 메뉴에서 안내자 만나기'.

HUD: pinned rows honor CanClaim/ShowProgress (HUD.luau:1979-1980, 2298, 2345-2357). The claim sends 'tutorial'. The step-1 guide beam goes to Pad_SlimeMeadow, then the gate, then the zone spawn. The travel menu includes SlimeMeadow (Config.Travel.Destinations). The blacksmith anvil exists in the place via tools/preview_map.lua, and ShopService sets BlacksmithVisited on the prompt.

Nil safety before data loads: every QuestService handler goes through getData. canWelcome only reaches getFaction after data is non-nil. getStep falls back to 99 without data. Client helpers default sensibly (WELCOME.Ready requires DataLoaded).

Init order: Main INIT_ORDER/START_ORDER start ZoneService, MonsterService and ShopService before QuestService, and PlayerService last. Net.CreateAll registers RequestTutorial/AcceptTutorial as RemoteEvents at runtime.
luau-compile exit 0 with no stderr for QuestService, DataService, Config, Net, Panels, HUD, MonsterService, ZoneService, Main.server, ShopService.

Offline fixture re-run in my scratch folder (repo untouched): tools/fixtures/onboarding_offline.luau against the current Config/DataService/QuestService/Net prints ONBOARDING_OFFLINE_OK checks=459. The SHAs in welcome_offline.json match the current QuestService, DataService, Net and fixture; only Config changed afterward. Coverage is server logic with test doubles only: no Panels/HUD, real MonsterService/ZoneService, live DataStore or multi-player.

Docs: SPEC_ADDENDUM A22 (first-mission bullet) and GDD §0-2 line 44 match the source-tree behaviour (3 pages, explicit accept, close ≠ accept, menu reopen, meadow, 5 slimes, 120 gold, no town slime). Player-facing text is Korean.
Firefly/Codex change: the first mission needs no new image generation. The welcome portrait reuses the existing Char<Faction>WarriorM parts, so this flow is not blocked by the subscription change.

findings.title: After the first reward, the player likely cannot afford the next weapon, and the pinned guidance ends at the shop visit

locations.quote: { Tier = 2, Damage = 15, Price = 150, MinLevel = 1,
QuestRewardGold = 120, -- existing first-hunt reward; no forced weapon purchase
if data.BlacksmithVisited ~= true then
-- The shop is a choice, not a prescribed next-tier purchase.

findings.explanation: Starting gold is 0 (Defaults BankGold/CarriedGold). The mission pays 120, and five Slime kills give 5 x 3 = 15 (Horns about 18), so roughly 135 gold. The tier-2 weapon costs 150. The only post-reward objective is '무기 살펴보기 · 교차로 마을 대장간'. Opening the shop sets BlacksmithVisited, after which tutorialEntry returns nil, and the fixture explicitly asserts no further pinned guidance. The old 'N마리 더!' affordability hint was removed: refreshUpgrade is now static and Config.Text.KillsToAfford/CanAfford are unused. The next guidance is the Lv10 GoblinWoods zone beam. Both GDD §0-2 line 24 (전리품 → 마을 상인 선택 → 다음 지역) and the 10-minute milestone in the persona expect an unbroken next action. This is arithmetic from Config, not a playtest.
findings.failure_scenario: A new player claims 120, walks to the Crossroads anvil, opens the shop with about 135 gold and sees the 150 wood weapon out of reach. The pinned row disappears and nothing says what to do next (hunt about 5 more slimes), so the first loop ends on an unaffordable item.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm in the 10-06 playtest. If confirmed, ask the user before changing the economy (reward or price is a design decision). A non-economic option is a second non-claimable pinned hint after the visit while the next tier is unaffordable (e.g. '슬라임 %d마리 더 사냥하면 나무 무기'), computed server-side, without reintroducing 'next unlock' teasers.
findings.verifier_note: The arithmetic holds and is a regression of this diff. Start gold is 0 (Config:72-73), tier 2 costs 150 (Config:157) and Slime gives Gold 3 (Config:881). In HEAD the personal golden slime paid 3×GoldenGoldMult 10 = 30 (MonsterService:1044), so the total was 120+30+15 = 165 ≥ 150; now it is about 135. Live evidence gameplay_10min/first_reward.json shows gold 120 + carried 18 = 138 after the reward, under the intermediate text '150골드를 모아… 부족하면 더 사냥해요', which has since been removed. The claim that nothing says what to do next is wrong. After BlacksmithVisited, the collapsed quest HUD falls back to the first claimable item, or else the first unfinished daily (HUD:2268-2282, e.g. '슬라임 50마리 쓰러뜨리기'). A Lv1 daily pays 180 gold (HuntValue 12×5×3), and a 'Release: 스킬 3번' daily is common, so many players clear 150 easily. The suggested 'N마리 더 → 나무 무기' hint risks conflicting with HANDOFF:9 '특정 다음 무기 구매를 강요하지 않는다' and Config:916 'no forced weapon purchase'. Treat this as a playtest pacing check.

findings.title: TutorialKills is never reset on acceptance, so a reset step with saved kills re-pays 120 gold instantly

locations.quote: setStep(player, STEP_GUIDE) -- acceptance in the meadow can enter step 2, without crediting any kill
if getTutorialKills(getData(player)) < TUT_TARGET then return end
S.PlayerService.SetStat(player, key, value)

findings.explanation: Kills can only accumulate at step 2, or on the step-1 meadow kill that moves to step 2, so at steps 0 and 1 the saved value should always be 0. Nothing enforces that. A scratch probe with a saved record {TutorialStep=0, TutorialKills=5} ran Accept, then ZoneTo meadow, then Claim: the step-2 row showed 5/5 at once and paid +120. No production code path writes step 0 or 1 after completion. The Studio DebugCommand (any mirrored stat, e.g. TutorialStep=0) or a manual DataStore edit does, which would make a QA re-test look instantly complete and pay twice.
findings.failure_scenario: A tester in Studio with API access invokes DebugCommand(player, 'TutorialStep', 0) to replay onboarding. After accepting and entering the meadow, the mission shows 5/5 and pays a second 120 gold without any kill.
findings.suggested_fix: In onAcceptTutorial, call S.PlayerService.SetStat(player, 'TutorialKills', 0) before setStep(STEP_GUIDE). Optionally, in DataService.fillDefaults, force TutorialKills = 0 when TutorialStep is 0 or 1. Add a fixture case saved(0,5) → accept → meadow → claim pays 0.
findings.verifier_note: QuestService:341-346 never resets TutorialKills, and claimTutorial (:382-385) only checks step 2 and kills ≥ 5. DataService:178-181 clamps kills but does not tie them to the step. The only writer of step 0/1 with saved kills > 0 is the Studio-only BindableFunction DebugCommand (Main:51-52 IsStudio guard, :94 generic SetStat) or a manual DataStore edit, which is not a client remote. So this is a QA hazard, not an exploit. Low is right.

dims.summary: Reviewed the blacksmith shop rewrite read-only: ShopService.luau (full file and git diff), DataService fillDefaults, Config (WeaponShop, Weapons, Vitals, RateLimits), Net, VitalsService/VitalsUI, MapBuilder, the Panels WeaponShop/Reconcile UI, HUD doUpgrade/refreshUpgrade, ProgressionService gold/rebirth, the QuestService visit objective, the Kaiju/Zone interactions, the place-file anvil hierarchy, and tools/gameplay_blacksmith_check.py with its evidence JSONs. The server-side trade core looks sound. Buy and sell re-check the real anchored anvil (12 studs), alive, ready and class chosen. The catalog is 1..3 with one integer argument. Debit, ownership bit and equip happen with no yield, sale pays floor(price*0.1) after clearing the bit, and the old UpgradeWeapon remote cannot bypass the town anvil. All ten touched Luau files compile with the offline luau-compile. Main problems: (1) the authoritative specs (AGENTS.md points to TECH_SPEC plus SPEC_ADDENDUM) still describe the old no-argument next-tier UpgradeWeapon and HUD card, and have no SellWeapon, WeaponOwnedMask or BlacksmithVisited contract. (2) The potion-merchant and NPC-art gates still require a GPT preview, but the user cancelled Codex on 2026-10-05 and moved to Adobe Firefly; no doc records this yet. (3) Rebirth resets WeaponTier but not WeaponOwnedMask, so weapons survive rebirth, against GDD §9. (4) Legacy rare tiers (4-7) stay in the ownership mask but can never be re-equipped once the player switches away. (5) With MerchantEnabled=false, potions cannot be obtained, yet the HUD and server text still point players to buying/using them. Smaller items: visits not recorded when trading from the U-key panel, a stuck client pending state, a kaiju able to spend raid-pool gold at the anvil, duplicated config constants, stale evidence hashes, and doc drift.
checked_ok: Proximity: ShopService.CanBuyWeapon (L178-192) resolves the exact workspace.Map(Folder)/Landmarks(Folder)/ArtisanGuild(Model)/Anvil(anchored BasePart). The server measures from the character's HumanoidRootPart position on the server against min(12, prompt.MaxActivationDistance) and requires Players parent, IsReady, Util.IsAlive and data.ClassChosen==true. Buy (L32) and sell (L105) both re-check this on every request. The place file confirms Workspace/Map/Landmarks/ArtisanGuild(Model)/Anvil(Part, Anchored=true) at (39,1.5,45), inside Crossroads (center 0, size 160, Town=true).

Prompt: EnsureBlacksmithPrompt is idempotent, uses key G (no Q/E collision) and HoldDuration 0.3. onBlacksmithPrompt rejects cloned or renamed prompts and is rate-limited. BlacksmithVisited is set only from the verified server prompt.

Buy: exactly one argument (select('#')==1). Tier must be an integer 1..Config.MaxWeaponTier, and MaxSoldTier is validated with a fail-closed refusal. Level gate and finite positive integer price are checked. SpendGold, then SetStat WeaponOwnedMask, then SetStat WeaponTier run with no yield in between, so a duplicate or delayed request finds the bit already owned and re-equips for free. Skip-ahead (direct tier 3) is allowed and does not grant tier 2. Tier 1 is equip-only (L62).

Sell: tiers 2..saleLimit only and owned only. Starter is unsellable (selectedTier<2). Proceeds = math.floor(price*0.1) = 15/80. The bit is cleared before AddCarriedGold. An equipped weapon falls back to tier 1. Nothing yields between check and write, so rapid duplicate or reentrant requests cannot double-pay. Source 'Sale' is ignored by QuestService.onGoldEarned (QuestService L777-780), so sale gold cannot farm the Gold quest.

Old UpgradeWeapon remote: still registered but now requires a tier argument plus anvil proximity. HUD doUpgrade (HUD L2644-2655) only opens the Travel/WeaponShop panel and a guide; no client path fires a next-tier purchase from the field. The old upgradeInfo/pulse code was removed from HUD.

Gold balance: ProgressionService.SpendGold spends CarriedGold (pocket, stealable) first, then BankGold (L223-242), which favors the player and matches GDD pocket-gold risk. The panel shows bank+pocket separately. Sale proceeds land in pocket while standing in Crossroads, which bankTick moves to the bank because Crossroads is a Town (ProgressionService L274-279).

DataService.fillDefaults: WeaponTier is handled as NaN/inf -> 1 and clamped. WeaponOwnedMask that is non-number, NaN, <1, >127 or fractional becomes 1, then bit32.bor(owned, 1, bit(tier)) keeps starter + equipped. Type-mismatched BlacksmithVisited is reset by the default loop. bit32 usage (lshift/band/bor/bnot with validMask 127) is correct.

Client merchant reaction: WSHOP.Reconcile marks Buy/Equip/Sell done only when the replicated WeaponOwnedMask/WeaponTier attributes show the change, so the farewell line reflects server-confirmed state. The client sell price math.floor(Price/10) equals the server's floor(price*0.1) for integer prices.

Visit objective refresh: I first suspected the pinned 'VisitBlacksmith' quest row would go stale after BlacksmithVisited flips. That is not the case: QuestService.tryTutorial marks step-99 players dirty every TUTORIAL_TICK=1s (QuestService L353-356, L940-948), so the row disappears within about 1.5 s.

Potion regression with MerchantEnabled=false: CanBuyPotions returns false first (ShopService L205). MapBuilder.ensurePotionMerchant disables any existing prompt and spawns nothing (L829). The place file has no PotionMerchant. VitalsService usePotion is unchanged and validates stock. BuyPotion debit and stock writes have no yield.

Net registers SellWeapon, and Config.RateLimits has SellWeapon=0.3. luau-compile exit 0 for ShopService, DataService, Config, Net, VitalsService, MapBuilder, Panels, HUD, ProgressionService and QuestService.

Offline fixture tools/gameplay_blacksmith_check.py covers payload fuzzing, distance and prompt tampering, NaN/neg/overflow masks, price corruption, duplicate/reentrant sale, skip-ahead and starter rules. It writes only to build/, not docs (I did not run it, per instructions). The ShopService hash in blacksmith_sale_offline.json matches the current file.

dims.summary:
I reviewed the six changed client modules (CameraFollow, HUD, Fx, Panels, ClassPicker, FactionPicker) against HEAD, plus ClientMain, UIKit, VitalsUI and Config.UIArt. All client files compile with the offline luau-compile 0.741. luau-analyze finds no unknown globals other than Roblox built-ins. Top-level locals stay well under 200; Fx is the closest at about 169.

The manual-combat input contract is implemented as written:
- A short world click fires one Swing on mouse release.
- A left drag only rotates the camera.
- Holding the mouse, F, R2 or the touch attack button sends exactly one Swing.
- GUI clicks and chat typing are filtered out.
- The charge, PERFECT, auto-attack and "next unlock" UI is fully gone, and no client code still calls SetAutoAttack.
- The skill button gates on SkillReadyAt (server time) and Mana >= 20.
- FactionPicker still uses the six approved FreshTyped IDs, and nothing in src references the rejected Aligned cards.

Bugs found: (1) For returning players, the HUD's blacksmith guide is cleared within about 1 second, and the shop window opens on top of the guide beam. (2) The left-drag camera never locks the mouse cursor. With shift-lock enabled in the place, holding the left button while moving the mouse adds a second rotation on top of Roblox's, and clicks made while the mouse moves are dropped instead of attacking. (3) On a 749x361 phone, the guide dialog's next/accept buttons sit below the visible area.

Rule conflicts the worker must not resolve alone:
- **Locked faction cards still advertise the removed charge gauge:** the approved FreshTyped cards still say "발사 게이지 175" (charge gauge 175) and "발사하면 동료 치유" (heal allies on release). Their SemanticText snapshot was edited to say the new text, which disables the guard that is supposed to catch exactly this.
- **Image pipeline:** AGENTS.md and RELEASE_PLAN.md still route all art through GPT/Codex, which was cancelled on 2026-10-05.
- **Language:** "Korean + English" conflicts with "Player-facing text is Korean", and the new UI hardcodes Korean strings.
- **Input-feel testing:** the required hands-on mouse/touch check can only be done by the user.

Lower items: the skill button shows no MP cost, there is no client potion-shop panel, plus stale comments and leftover code.
checked_ok: Offline compile: CameraFollow, HUD, Fx, Panels, ClassPicker, FactionPicker, UIKit, VitalsUI, WorldMap, EventHUD and ClientMain.client.luau all exit 0 with no stderr from build/luau_cli_0_741/luau-compile.exe. luau-analyze --mode=nonstrict reports no unknown globals other than Roblox built-ins; only lints are unused locals (HUD: Net import, playSound, swingInterval, token).

Top-level locals, counted approximately by a script (column-0 'local' names): HUD 148 (HEAD 165), Fx 169 (HEAD 174), Panels 136 (HEAD 134), ClassPicker 124, FactionPicker 128, CameraFollow 29. All under 200, and luau-compile would have raised a register error otherwise.

Mouse click vs drag (CameraFollow.luau:36-65): Swing fires only on MouseButton1 release, and only if Held, not Moved (6 px), not gameProcessed and not blocked(). blocked() covers the Roblox menu, a focused TextBox, DataLoaded, the pickers, Panels and WorldMap, a non-Custom camera and a missing character. Clicks on HUD TextButtons/ArtButtons are processed, so they never double-fire with ui.attack.InputBegan. RMB cancels the left drag and stays with the default camera.

No repeat attacks: HUD startHold (HUD.luau:2613-2623) sends one Swing and the task.spawn repeat loop is gone. holdSources prevents re-firing while any source is still held. Releases are handled even when gameProcessed, and clearHolds runs on focus loss, HUD hide and respawn. F/R2/touch/mouse-on-button each send exactly one Swing per press.

Keyboard input is ignored when gameProcessed (chat typing). The R/auto key and MouseButton1 startHold were removed. The Q/E/L2 skill keys do not collide with ProximityPrompts (blacksmith, altar and potion prompts use G).

Touch: world taps do not attack (Touch is not handled by CameraFollow); touch camera drag and thumbstick stay with the default PlayerModule. Attack button is 136 and skill button 102 logical units (~102/77 real px at UIScale 0.75); the squares are 72.

Removed UI: no remaining references to ui.auto, ui.ring, ui.charge*, perfectOn, recentGold, afford, refreshCharge, refreshPerfect, refreshAuto or toggleAuto. No client reads Charge, ChargeCap, PerfectUntil or AutoAttack, and no client fires SetAutoAttack. The Fx Release handler no longer shows PERFECT or auto-release text; Fx level-up no longer shows next-unlock toasts; ClassPicker intro toasts that mentioned the charge gauge are removed.

Skill button (HUD.luau:1869-1881, 2634-2642): readiness comes from SkillReadyAt minus Util.Now() (workspace:GetServerTimeNow, matching the server's Util.Now()+cooldown) and Mana >= Config.BasicSkill.ManaCost (20). The countdown replaces the icon. Pressing with low MP shows a 'MP가 부족해요.' toast; during cooldown the press is ignored silently.

Welcome dialog (Panels.luau:1151-1218, 2031-2066): 'later' and X never accept; accept sends a zero-argument AcceptTutorial with a 5 s retry message; closing clears PendingOpen; the menu entry '안내자 만나기' matches the quest text in Config.Tutorial.Text.Welcome. The portrait reuses the existing Char<Faction>WarriorM art; I viewed all three source PNGs and they are fully clothed and modest.

WeaponShop panel (Panels.luau:1693-1924): Korean text; display-side checks mirror the server (anvil path, prompt enabled, 12-stud 3D distance, tier cap 3, owned mask); selling requires confirmation; a stale 'equip' click cannot turn into a paid purchase; the farewell line only appears on a manual close. Fired remotes UpgradeWeapon/SellWeapon(tier) match the ShopService handlers.

FactionPicker uses Config.UIArt.FactionE.Parts, which maps to FactionCardHaloFreshTyped 76818879022385, Horns 137806621328187, Neutral 127475794518664, Title 81044633324158, Premise 105024415024705 and Footer 128423642459976. 'Aligned' appears only in art/approved.json with status rejected_design_changed / active:false; nothing in src references it.

Connections and nil-safety: CameraFollow, HUD and Panels connect global signals once in Start. Per-character connections are disconnected on rebind. WSHOP.Access, isDead, updateSubject and showGuide all handle a missing character, root or anvil safely. ClientMain requires every module before Init, so CameraFollow's registry and HUD.Start's C.CameraFollow.PrimaryClick both resolve.
No keyboard-only actions on mobile: attack, skill, map, menu and the shop card are buttons; potions are VitalsUI buttons; the blacksmith ProximityPrompt is tappable; all Panels actions are buttons.
Server Fx kinds (Bank, GooseEnd, Hurt, LevelUp, Pain, Plunder, Rare, Rebirth, Reward, Stomp, Upgrade, plus Swing/Release via the generic send) all still have client handlers.

findings.title: Returning players' blacksmith guide (HUD card / U key) is cleared within ~1 s, and the shop modal opens over it

locations.quote: elseif guide.Tag == "blacksmith" and (attr("BlacksmithVisited", false) == true or zone ~= "Crossroads") then
showGuide(L.BlacksmithTarget(), "대장간 · 모루와 상호작용", "blacksmith", nil)
panels.Open("WeaponShop")
WeaponFar = "대장간 모루 가까이에서 무기를 살펴볼 수 있어요.",

findings.explanation: In Crossroads, doUpgrade (the always-visible '장비 상인' card or the U key) shows a guide tagged "blacksmith" and then immediately opens the WeaponShop panel. refreshGuides runs every 5 ticks (1 s). For any player with BlacksmithVisited == true it destroys a "blacksmith" guide, so the beam the card just created disappears within about a second for every returning visitor. Meanwhile the WeaponShop modal (a full-screen, Active, dark backdrop) covers the beam. When the player is more than 12 studs from the anvil, the modal only shows the WeaponFar message. The card's promise of directions ('대장간에서 구입 · 길 안내' wording and the guide call) is therefore never delivered after the first visit.
findings.failure_scenario: A player who already used the anvil once is in Crossroads, far from the guild, and clicks the 장비 상인 card. The modal shows '대장간 모루 가까이에서…'. The player closes it, and the gold beam to the anvil is already gone (cleared on the next 1 s refreshGuides), so there is no direction to the shop.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the on-demand guide its own tag (for example "blacksmith-manual") that is cleared only when the player reaches the anvil or leaves Crossroads, not when BlacksmithVisited is true. When WSHOP.Access() would return WeaponFar, consider only showing the guide plus a toast instead of opening the modal.
findings.verifier_note: The core bug is real. doUpgrade (HUD.luau:2653-2654) shows a guide tagged 'blacksmith' and opens WeaponShop. refreshGuides (HUD.luau:2559) clears that guide whenever BlacksmithVisited==true. It runs every 5 ticks of TICK=0.2 (HUD.luau:38, 2951-2957), and runs while Panels is open because refreshVisibility only checks the pickers (HUD.luau:2927). Returning players therefore lose the beam within about 1 s. Correction: the card does not say '대장간에서 구입 · 길 안내'. That string is the unused TXT.UpgradeReady (HUD.luau:156). The visible card text is '장비 상인 / 무기 선택 · 구매 · 판매 / 교차로 마을 대장간' (HUD.luau:1908-1910). The modal backdrop is semi-transparent (BackgroundTransparency 0.45, Panels.luau:860), so it does not fully hide the beam.

findings.title: Left-drag camera does not lock the cursor and stacks with shift-lock rotation; clicks while the mouse moves are dropped

locations.quote: if processed or blocked() then cancelDrag(); return end
if drag.Distance >= DRAG_THRESHOLD then drag.Moved = true end
camera.CFrame = CFrame.new(camera.CFrame.Position) * rotation
<bool name="EnableMouseLockOption">true</bool>

findings.explanation: CameraFollow never sets UserInputService.MouseBehavior (no MouseBehavior anywhere in src). This creates three problems. (a) During a left drag the cursor moves freely: rotation stops at the screen edge, and when the cursor crosses an Active GUI element the MouseMovement event is likely flagged processed, which cancels the drag. Roblox's own right-mouse orbit avoids this by locking the cursor in place (LockCurrentPosition). (b) The place enables shift-lock. In shift-lock or first-person (LockCenter), Roblox already rotates the camera on every mouse movement. CameraFollow adds the same deltas again whenever the left button is held, so the camera turns at double speed. (c) In those modes, a click whose cumulative path length reaches 6 px is classified as a drag, so attacking while aiming silently does nothing. A22/GDD 0-2 require left-drag rotation and short-click attacks, and direct mouse feel is still unverified.
findings.failure_scenario: A PC player turns on shift-lock and clicks to attack while turning toward a slime. The mouse moves at least 6 px during the click, so no Swing is sent, and the camera spins twice as fast while the button is held. Without shift-lock, a long left drag stops rotating when the cursor reaches the screen edge or passes over the quest panel.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the custom drag (but still emit the click) when UserInputService.MouseBehavior is LockCenter. Set MouseBehavior to LockCurrentPosition once drag.Moved becomes true and restore it on release or cancel. Consider ignoring `processed` on MouseMovement after the drag has started. Then verify by hand with the user (see client-ui-12).
findings.verifier_note: All four quotes are at the cited lines. src/ never sets MouseBehavior. EnableMouseLockOption=true is the Roblox default, not a deliberate choice. CameraMinZoomDistance 0.5 (place/GoodEvil.rbxlx:122657) also allows first-person LockCenter. Point (c) is certain from the code: cumulative path >= 6 px means drag.Moved, and onPrimaryEnded then emits no click (CameraFollow.luau:55, 60). Points (a) and (b) depend on engine behavior: whether MouseMovement is marked processed over GUI, and the double rotation in LockCenter. Both are plausible but not verified in the engine.

findings.explanation: Config.UIArt.FactionE.SemanticText is the snapshot of what the baked approved images actually say. E.semantic shows the baked image only when that snapshot equals the live perk text, which is the guard against stale baked wording. The uncommitted diff rewrote both the live perk text and the snapshot to '약탈한 골드 지켜내기' / '스킬로 동료 치유'. The approved PNGs (art/ui/UIP_FactionCardHorns_FreshTyped.png and UIP_FactionCardHalo_FreshTyped.png, both viewed) still say '발사 게이지 175' and '발사하면 동료 치유'. The guard therefore passes and every new player sees a removed mechanic on the first screen, while the code records otherwise. These rules conflict: the cards are locked ('Approved design stays fixed'), A22 explicitly lets old card text remain, and the persona says not to advertise features that do not exist. A worker could 'fix' this either by restoring the honest snapshot, which makes the semantic check fail and swaps in the code-drawn fallback (changing approved art), or by editing the art (forbidden).
findings.failure_scenario: A new player picks 뿔 군단 because of '발사 게이지 175'; no charge gauge exists in the game. Later, a worker sees the SemanticText says '약탈한 골드 지켜내기' and believes the card was already updated.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not change the art or toggle the fallback without asking. Restore SemanticText to the true baked wording, or add a comment that it intentionally diverges, and ask the user in Korean whether to (a) accept the old card text until the redraw or (b) approve new lettering for those two rows only. That lettering now has to be made with Firefly (see client-ui-04).
findings.verifier_note: The facts are real. The SemanticText snapshot (Config.luau:1464-1476) was edited to '스킬로 동료 치유' / '약탈한 골드 지켜내기' with no comment. The approved PNGs still read '발사하면 동료 치유' / '발사 게이지 175' (I viewed both). E.semantic therefore passes (FactionPicker.luau:516-520). The claimed rule conflict is already settled, though: SPEC_ADDENDUM.md:10 (A22, latest contract) says '카드 그림 속 옛 문구는 디자인 후순위로 남을 수 있고, 이를 고쳤다고 보고하거나 승인 아트를 임의 교체하지 않는다'. The AGENTS quote is at line 31, not 27, and it is about rewards. What remains is a misleading snapshot that hides the stale baked text, plus a removed mechanic shown on the Horns card.

findings.title: "Korean + English in one experience" conflicts with "Player-facing text is Korean"; new UI hardcodes Korean strings

locations.quote: Languages: Korean + English in one experience.
Player-facing text is Korean.
`LocalizationTable`: 한국어 원문 → 영어 번역을 직접 넣는다.

findings.explanation: The coding convention tells the worker to write player-facing text in Korean, while the release plan requires ko+en via LocalizationTable before the 10/24 cutline (or 12/19). The new code follows the convention with literal Korean strings. Some sit outside any text table (HUD refreshUpgrade literals, toasts in doRelease/doUpgrade); others are in Panels.T and Config.Tutorial.Welcome. Many are string.format results ('가격 %s골드 · 필요 Lv %d…'), which Roblox auto-localization cannot match exactly. FactionE baked text is Korean-only, and E.semantic deliberately returns false for non-'ko' locales. Each new screen built this way adds localization debt, and the worker gets no instruction on how to write strings for later translation.
findings.failure_scenario: During the English pass, formatted strings such as WeaponPriceF and Welcome lines do not match LocalizationTable source entries, so English players see mixed Korean/English in the first-play dialog and the shop.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask the user to confirm the rule: Korean source text written so it can be localized (central text tables, Translator:FormatByKey for formatted strings). Update AGENTS.md line 56 accordingly, and keep the English cutline from RELEASE_PLAN.
findings.verifier_note: This is not a real rule conflict. RELEASE_PLAN.md:30 '한국어 원문 → 영어 번역' fits AGENTS.md:56 'Player-facing text is Korean' (Korean source, translated through LocalizationTable). The real remaining point is localization debt from string.format and literal strings outside text tables. English may slip to 12/19 under the cutline (RELEASE_PLAN.md:35), so this is low for the beta. The quotes at HUD.luau:1908, 2638 and Config.luau:1440 are accurate.
